selection_process: Stage I: computer based test → Stage II: physical fitness test, assessment & adaptability test, document verification, recruitment medical → Stage III: document check & pre-enrolment medical at INS Chilka → Stage IV: verification of original documents with boards

aliases: CA Foundation; ICAI Foundation; Chartered Accountant Foundation; CA entrance
forms_out: About 2 months before each exam (e.g. early July for September)
marking: Papers 3 & 4 (objective): -0.25 per wrong answer; Papers 1 & 2 descriptive
eligibility: You can register for the Foundation Course after passing Class 10, but you can sit the exam only after appearing in the Class 12 board exam (any recognised board). Registration must be done at least four months before the exam month (by 1 Sept for January, 1 Jan for May, 1 May for September). Registration is valid for 4 years from the first eligible attempt. No age limit. Commerce graduates with 55% or other graduates with 60% (and ICSI/ICMAI Intermediate passes) are exempt from Foundation and can go straight to Intermediate.
last_date: About 2 months before each exam (e.g. mid/late July for September)
test_date: January, May and September (three times a year)
application_fee: Rs. 9,000/- one-time Foundation Course registration (includes study material); exam fee Rs. 1,500/- per attempt (India centres), late fee Rs. 600/-
paper_pattern: Four papers of 100 marks each (400 total): Paper 1 Accounting and Paper 2 Business Laws (descriptive, 3 hours each); Paper 3 Quantitative Aptitude (Business Mathematics, Logical Reasoning, Statistics) and Paper 4 Business Economics (objective MCQ on OMR, 2 hours each, 0.25 negative marking). English or Hindi medium.
remarks: Pass needs 40% in each paper and 50% aggregate in one sitting; there is no paper-wise exemption at Foundation. CA is a professional course run by ICAI, not a college degree.
selection_process: Foundation exam (4 papers) → Intermediate (2 groups, 6 papers) → ICITSS (4 weeks) → Articleship / practical training (2 years) → Advanced ICITSS + Self-Paced Online Modules → Final exam (2 groups, 6 papers)

aliases: CA Intermediate; CA Inter; ICAI Intermediate; CA IPCC (old name)
forms_out: About 2 months before each exam (e.g. early July for September)
marking: 30 marks of MCQs per paper, no negative marking; 70 marks descriptive
eligibility: Two routes. (1) Foundation route: pass CA Foundation (taken after Class 12), then register for Intermediate. (2) Direct entry route: commerce graduates/post-graduates with at least 55%, other graduates/post-graduates with at least 60%, or those who passed ICSI/ICMAI Intermediate; final-year graduates can register provisionally. Either way you must complete 8 months of study after registering before the exam (register by 1 Jan for September, 1 May of the previous year for January, 1 Sept of the previous year for May). Registration is valid 5 years. No age limit.
last_date: About 2 months before each exam (e.g. mid/late July for September)
test_date: January, May and September (three times a year)
application_fee: Rs. 18,000/- one-time Intermediate Course registration (both groups); exam fee Rs. 1,500/- for one group or Rs. 2,700/- for both groups (India centres), late fee Rs. 600/-
paper_pattern: Six papers of 100 marks each in two groups. Group I: Advanced Accounting; Corporate and Other Laws; Taxation (Income-tax 50 + GST 50). Group II: Cost and Management Accounting; Auditing and Ethics; Financial Management and Strategic Management (50 + 50). Each paper 3 hours, 30% case-based MCQs and 70% descriptive.
remarks: You can take one group or both groups in a sitting. To pass a group you need 40% in each paper and 50% aggregate; 60% in a paper gives an exemption for the next three attempts. Passing both groups (plus ICITSS) lets you start the 2-year articleship.
selection_process: Foundation exam (4 papers) → Intermediate (2 groups, 6 papers) → ICITSS (4 weeks) → Articleship / practical training (2 years) → Advanced ICITSS + Self-Paced Online Modules → Final exam (2 groups, 6 papers)

application_fee: Rs. 500/- (Rs. 400/- refunded on appearing in 1st stage CBT); Rs. 250/- for SC, ST, ex-servicemen, PwBD, women, transgender, minorities and EBC (fully refunded, less bank charges, on appearing in 1st stage CBT)
paper_pattern: 1st stage CBT: 100 objective questions of 1 mark each in 90 minutes - General Awareness 40, Mathematics 30, General Intelligence and Reasoning 30 (section split is indicative). 1/3 mark deducted per wrong answer. 2nd stage CBT: 120 questions in 90 minutes (General Awareness 50, Mathematics 35, Reasoning 35).
remarks: Posts in CEN 06/2026: Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor, Goods Train Manager, Junior Accounts Assistant cum Typist, Senior Clerk cum Typist (Pay Level 5-6). Station Master is not in CEN 06/2026 and the typing test was dropped; posts change every notification, so check the CEN.
selection_process: 1st stage CBT → 2nd stage CBT → Document verification & medical examination

exam_name: RRB Group D (Railway Recruitment Board Level 1 Posts)
aliases: RRB Group D; Railway Group D; RRB Level 1; RRC Group D; Track Maintainer; Pointsman; Railway Level-1 posts
eligibility: Class 10 pass, or ITI, or equivalent, or National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) from NCVT. Age 18-33 years (as on 1 January 2026 for CEN 09/2025). Age relaxation exists for SC/ST, OBC (NCL), PwBD, ex-servicemen and others. Citizens of Nepal and Bhutan and some other categories can also apply as per the CEN.
application_fee: Rs. 500/- (Rs. 400/- refunded on appearing in CBT); Rs. 250/- for SC, ST, ex-servicemen, PwBD, women, transgender, minorities and EBC (fully refunded, less bank charges, on appearing in CBT)
paper_pattern: Single CBT: 100 objective questions of 1 mark each in 90 minutes - General Science 25, Mathematics 25, General Intelligence and Reasoning 30, General Awareness and Current Affairs 20 (indicative). 1/3 mark deducted per wrong answer. Minimum marks: UR/EWS 40%, OBC/SC/ST 30%.
remarks: PET: men lift 35 kg for 100 m in 2 minutes and run 1000 m in 4 min 15 s; women lift 20 kg for 100 m in 2 minutes and run 1000 m in 5 min 40 s. Posts include Track Maintainer, Pointsman and various Assistant posts at Pay Level 1.
selection_process: CBT → Physical Efficiency Test (PET) → Document verification & medical examination

aliases: RRB ALP; Railway ALP; Assistant Loco Pilot; Railway Loco Pilot recruitment; RRB Loco Pilot
eligibility: Class 10 (Matriculation/SSLC) plus ITI from NCVT/SCVT in a listed trade (e.g. Fitter, Electrician, Mechanic Diesel, Turner, Machinist), or Class 10 plus Course Completed Act Apprenticeship in those trades, or Class 10 plus a 3-year diploma (or degree) in Mechanical/Electrical/Electronics/Automobile Engineering. Class 10 alone is not enough. Age 18-30 years (as on 1 July 2026 for CEN 01/2026); relaxations exist for SC/ST, OBC (NCL), ex-servicemen and others. Medical standard A-1 (strict eyesight); not suitable for PwBD.
application_fee: Rs. 500/- (Rs. 400/- refunded on appearing in CBT-1); Rs. 250/- for SC, ST, ex-servicemen, women, transgender, minorities and EBC (fully refunded, less bank charges, on appearing in CBT-1)
paper_pattern: CBT-1 (screening only): 75 objective questions of 1 mark in 60 minutes on Mathematics, Mental Ability and General Science (Class 10 level); 1/3 mark deducted per wrong answer. CBT-2: Part A 100 questions in 90 minutes, Part B (trade, qualifying 35%) 75 questions in 60 minutes.
remarks: Final merit uses CBT-2 Part A and CBAT scores 50:50; CBAT has no negative marking and each test battery must be cleared. Candidates must pass a strict A-1 medical (vision) standard.
selection_process: CBT-1 (screening) → CBT-2 (Part A + trade Part B) → Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT) → Document verification & medical examination

aliases: IBPS PO; IBPS PO/MT; CRP PO/MT; IBPS Probationary Officer; Bank PO; IBPS Management Trainee
marking: 1/4 of the question's marks deducted per wrong answer; no penalty for unanswered questions
eligibility: A degree (graduation) in any discipline from a recognised university, with the result declared by the closing date of registration (21.07.2026 in the 2026 cycle). Age 20 to 30 years as on 01.07.2026 (born 02.07.1996 to 01.07.2006); upper age relaxations exist for SC/ST (5 years), OBC-NCL (3 years), PwBD (10 years), ex-servicemen and others.

Candidates must clear the cut-off in each section. Mains has 170 objective questions for 200 marks (Reasoning; General/Economy/Banking/Digital/Financial Awareness; English; Data Analysis & Interpretation) in 160 minutes, plus a 25-mark descriptive paper (essay and comprehension) in 30 minutes.
remarks: One common exam for PO/MT posts in 11 public sector banks (excluding SBI); vacancies are indicative and are updated by corrigenda during the cycle. Confirm the latest figures on ibps.in.
selection_process: Prelims (objective, qualifying) → Mains (objective + descriptive) → Personality Test (non-qualifying, compulsory) → Interview (Mains:Interview weightage 80:20) → Provisional allotment to a participating bank

aliases: IBPS Clerk; IBPS CSA; CRP CSA; CRP Clerical Cadre; IBPS Customer Service Associate; Bank Clerk
marking: +1/-0.25 in Prelims (1/4 of the question's marks deducted per wrong answer; no penalty for unanswered questions)
eligibility: A degree (graduation) in any discipline from a recognised university, held on the day of registration; computer literacy (certificate/diploma/degree in computers or computers studied as a subject in school/college). Must be able to read, write, speak and understand the official local language of the State/UT applied for. Age 20 to 28 years as on 01.08.2026 (born 02.08.1998 to 01.08.2006); upper age relaxations exist for SC/ST, OBC-NCL, PwBD, ex-servicemen and others.
test_date: Prelims in October; Mains in December

Candidates must clear the cut-off in each section. Mains has 160 questions for 200 marks in 125 minutes (General/Financial Awareness, General English, Reasoning Ability, Quantitative Aptitude). Tests other than English are offered in Hindi and the regional language of many States.
remarks: Candidates apply for vacancies in one State/UT and must know its local language; there is no interview. Vacancies are indicative and are revised during the cycle, so check ibps.in.
selection_process: Prelims (objective, qualifying) → Mains (objective; final merit on Mains marks only) → Local Language Proficiency Test (qualifying) → Provisional allotment to a participating bank

aliases: SBI PO; SBI Probationary Officer; State Bank of India PO; Bank PO

Age 21 to 30 years as on 01.04.2026 (born 02.04.1996 to 01.04.2005); upper age relaxations exist for OBC (3 years), SC/ST (5 years), PwBD (10 to 15 years) and ex-servicemen.

No sectional cut-off; about 10 times the vacancies are shortlisted for Mains. Mains (2026) has 170 objective questions for 200 marks in 3 hours plus a 30-mark descriptive test (communication skills) in 30 minutes.
remarks: SBI runs its own PO exam, separate from IBPS PO. Selected candidates sign a service bond and can be posted anywhere in India.
selection_process: Prelims (objective, qualifying) → Mains (objective + descriptive) → Psychometric test → Group exercise & interview (50 marks) → Final merit (Mains 75% + GE/interview 25%)

exam_name: SBI Clerk (Junior Associate - Customer Support & Sales)
aliases: SBI Clerk; SBI Junior Associate; SBI JA; SBI Customer Support & Sales; State Bank of India Clerk
marking: +1/-0.25 (1/4 of the question's marks deducted per wrong answer)

test_date: Prelims in September; Mains in November

No sectional or aggregate minimum; about 10 times the vacancies are shortlisted for Mains. Mains has 190 questions for 200 marks in 2 hours 40 minutes (General/Financial Awareness, General English, Quantitative Aptitude, Reasoning & Computer Aptitude).
remarks: Apply for one State/UT only; there is no inter-state transfer for 5 years. A separate special drive for SC/ST/OBC backlog posts may run alongside the main notification.
selection_process: Prelims (objective, qualifying) → Mains (objective; final merit on Mains marks) → Local Language Proficiency Test (qualifying) → Document verification & joining

exam_name: APPSC Group 1 (Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission Group-I Services Examination)
aliases: APPSC Group I; AP Group 1; Andhra Pradesh Group 1 Services; APPSC Deputy Collector exam
mode: Pen & Paper Based (objective prelims; descriptive mains)
eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university (some posts need a specific degree, e.g. DSP Communications needs B.E./B.Tech in ECE or related). Age 18 to 42 years, raised to 44 for non-uniformed posts by G.O.Ms.No.187 (valid to 30 Sep 2027); DSP posts have lower upper limits. Relaxations for SC/ST/BC (5 years) and PwBD (10 years). Candidates from any state may apply, but non-local candidates compete only in open (unreserved) seats; local status needs AP certificates.
last_date: As per notification (2026 cycle: 9 November 2026 after extension)
test_date: As per notification (2026 cycle prelims: 24 January 2027)
application_fee: Rs. 370/- (Rs. 250/- processing + Rs. 120/- exam fee); SC/ST/BC/PwBD/ex-servicemen, white ration card holders and unemployed youth of AP pay only Rs. 250/-
paper_pattern: Prelims (screening only) has two objective papers of 120 questions, 120 marks and 120 minutes each: Paper I General Studies (history and culture, polity, economy, geography) and Paper II General Aptitude (mental ability, science and technology, current events). Available in English and Telugu. Prelims marks do not count for final merit; about 50 candidates per post go to Mains.
remarks: Final merit is out of 825 (750 Mains + 75 interview). Posts and vacancies change every notification; confirm on psc.ap.gov.in.
selection_process: Prelims (objective, screening) → Mains (5 descriptive papers of 150 marks + qualifying Telugu and English papers) → Interview (75 marks) → Document verification

exam_name: APPSC CCE (Arunachal Pradesh Public Service Combined Competitive Examination)
aliases: APPSCCE; Arunachal PSC CCE; Arunachal Pradesh Civil Service exam; APCS exam
eligibility: Graduate degree from a recognised university (final-year students may apply provisionally). Open only to citizens who are permanent residents of Arunachal Pradesh (PRC) and hold an Arunachal Pradesh Scheduled Tribe (APST) certificate, and who can speak an indigenous tribal language of the state (2026 rule). Age 21 to 35 years on the last date of application (20 Oct 2026); relaxation of 5 years for APST, more for PwBD and disabled defence personnel.
test_date: As per notification (2026 cycle prelims: 6 December 2026; 2024 cycle: 15 December 2024)
paper_pattern: Prelims has two objective papers of 200 marks and 2 hours each, set in English: Paper I General Studies (decides who goes to Mains) and Paper II Aptitude Test (CSAT), which is qualifying with 33% needed. About 12 times the number of vacancies are admitted to Mains. Prelims marks do not count for final merit.
remarks: Only APST permanent residents of Arunachal Pradesh are eligible from the 2026 cycle. The exam is not held every year (the 2024 cycle came after a gap of about four years).
selection_process: Prelims (objective, screening) → Mains (8 descriptive papers incl. qualifying English) → Interview (275 marks) → Document verification & medical (physical tests for police posts)

exam_name: APSC CCE (Assam Public Service Commission Combined Competitive Examination)
aliases: APSC CCE; Assam PSC; Assam Civil Service exam; ACS exam; APSC prelims
eligibility: Degree from a recognised university. Indian citizen, original inhabitant of Assam, registered in a District Employment Office of Assam, and able to speak Assamese or another official/associate official language or a tribal language of the state. Age 21 to 38 years on 1 Jan 2025 (CCE 2025); relaxed by 5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC/MOBC and 10 years for PwBD.
test_date: As per notification (CCE 2025 prelims: 5 July 2026; CCE 2024 prelims: 8 June 2025)
application_fee: Rs. 297.20/- (General: Rs. 250/- + Rs. 47.20/- processing); OBC/MOBC Rs. 197.20/-; SC/ST, BPL, PwBD and all women pay only the Rs. 47.20/- processing fee
paper_pattern: Prelims has two objective papers of 200 marks and 2 hours each: General Studies I (30-35% of questions on Assam) and General Studies II, which is qualifying (33% needed). Prelims is screening only; marks do not count for final merit. Papers were set in Assamese and English in 2026.
remarks: Mains is held only in Guwahati. Vacancies vary sharply between cycles (262 in CCE 2024, 78 in CCE 2025); confirm on apsc.nic.in.
selection_process: Prelims (objective, screening) → Mains (6 descriptive papers, 1,500 marks: Essay, GS I-IV, Assam paper) → Interview (180 marks) → Document verification

exam_name: BPSC CCE (Bihar Public Service Commission Combined Competitive Examination)
aliases: BPSC; BPSC 71st CCE; Bihar PCS; BPSC Integrated CCE; Bihar civil services exam
eligibility: Bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised university. Minimum age 21 years (varies by post); maximum 37 years for general men, 40 for general women and BC/EBC, 42 for SC/ST (71st CCE, age counted on 1 Aug 2025 per aggregators). Reservation and fee concessions are only for Bihar residents; other-state candidates compete as general category.
application_fee: Rs. 600/- (Rs. 150/- for SC/ST of Bihar, women who are Bihar residents, and PwD); plus Rs. 200/- biometric fee
paper_pattern: Prelims is one objective General Studies paper of 150 questions, 150 marks, 2 hours. It is screening only; about 10 times the vacancies are called to Mains.
remarks: One of the largest state PSC exams by applicants. Posts and vacancies change every notification and are often revised upward after the advert; confirm on bpsc.bihar.gov.in.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (General Hindi qualifying + General Studies and essay papers, descriptive) → Interview (120 marks) → Document verification

exam_name: CGPSC SSE (Chhattisgarh Public Service Commission State Service Examination)

marking: +2/-0.67 (1/3 of marks deducted per wrong answer)

Age 21 to 30 years on 1 Jan 2025 for most posts; Chhattisgarh domicile candidates may be up to 35 (+5 years for educated unemployed of CG); DSP 21 to 28. SC/ST/OBC of CG get 5 more years, CG women 10 more, with a combined cap of 45. Reservation only for CG domicile; others compete as unreserved.
application_fee: Rs. 400/- (Rs. 300/- for Chhattisgarh-domicile SC/ST/OBC non-creamy layer and PwD), plus portal fee and GST; CG-domicile candidates who appear in the written exam/interview can claim an exam fee refund
paper_pattern: Prelims has two objective papers of 100 questions, 200 marks and 2 hours each: Paper I General Studies (decides Mains shortlist, about 15 times vacancies) and Paper II Aptitude Test (qualifying). Minimum 33% (23% reserved) in each paper.
remarks: Mains Language paper and Essay include Chhattisgarh-specific content. Posts and vacancies change every notification; confirm on psc.cg.gov.in.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (7 descriptive papers of 200 marks: Language, Essay, GS I-V; 1,400 marks) → Interview (100 marks) → Document verification

exam_name: Goa PSC JSO (Goa Public Service Commission Junior Scale Officer, Goa Civil Service Recruitment)
aliases: Goa PSC; GPSC Goa; Goa Civil Service; Junior Scale Officer Goa; GCS exam
mode: Computer Based (pre-screening and screening CBRT); written exam and interview after that
eligibility: Degree from a recognised university. Knowledge of Konkani is essential (Marathi desirable). Age not more than 40 years on the last date of application; government may relax for certain categories, but never beyond 50.
paper_pattern: Pre-screening test: 60 MCQs, 60 marks, 75 minutes (50 marks reasoning and numerical aptitude, 10 marks English comprehension), no negative marking; pass mark 65% for General/EWS, 60% OBC/PwD, 55% SC/ST, with a repeat test for borderline scores. Then a screening CBRT of 75 marks in 90 minutes (polity, history, geography, environment, current affairs, English, reasoning).
remarks: Goa does not hold a regular yearly combined state civil services exam; GPSC advertises Junior Scale Officer (Goa Civil Service) posts on its own from time to time. Watch gpsc.goa.gov.in for the next advertisement.
selection_process: Pre-screening test (CBRT) → Screening test (CBRT, 75 marks) → Competitive written exam (250 marks) → Oral interview (40 marks) → Final merit on written + interview

exam_name: GPSC Class 1-2 (Gujarat Public Service Commission Gujarat Administrative Service and Civil Services Class 1 & 2 Combined Competitive Examination)

eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university (final-year students may sit prelims). Age 20 to 35 years; upper age relaxed for SC/ST/SEBC/EWS (to 40 for men, 45 for women), unreserved women (40), PwBD (45) and ex-servicemen.
test_date: As per notification (2026 cycle prelims: 7 June 2026; mains October 2026)

selection_process: Prelims (objective, qualifying) → Mains (Gujarati and English qualifying papers + 5 essay/GS papers, 1,250 marks) → Personality test (150 marks) → Document verification

Upper age relaxed 5 years for SC and BC of Haryana, and for PwBD, widows and some other groups; reserved-category benefits only for Haryana residents.
test_date: As per notification (latest prelims: 26 April 2026; Mains 27-29 June 2026)
application_fee: Rs. 1000/- (Rs. 250/- for DSC, OSC, BC-A, BC-B, ESM, EWS and women of Haryana; no fee for PwBD of Haryana)

selection_process: Prelims (objective, screening) → Mains (6 descriptive papers of 100 marks: English, Hindi, GS I-IV) → Personality test / viva-voce (75 marks) → Final merit on 675 marks

remarks: Few posts are offered each year. Confirm all details in the official notification on hppsc.hp.gov.in.
selection_process: Prelims → Mains (written) → Interview

remarks: Only J&K domicile holders can apply. Confirm all details on jkpsc.nic.in.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (8 written papers) → Interview (250 marks)

exam_name: JPSC CCE (Jharkhand Public Service Commission Combined Civil Services Examination)

eligibility: Degree from a recognised university. test_date: As per notification (CCE 2025 prelims: 19 April 2026; Mains 18-20 July 2026)

selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (6 descriptive papers: qualifying Hindi & English 100 + Language & Literature 150 + 4 GS papers of 200; 950 marks) → Interview (100 marks) → Final merit on 1,050 marks

exam_name: KPSC KAS (Karnataka Gazetted Probationers Group A & B Combined Competitive Examination)
aliases: KAS; Karnataka Administrative Service; KPSC Gazetted Probationers; Karnataka PCS
forms_out: As per notification (2026 cycle: notified 31 July, applications in August)

application_fee: Rs. 600/- (Rs. 300/- for categories 2A/2B/3A/3B; Rs. 50/- for ex-servicemen; no fee for SC/ST/Category-1/PwD) (2026 cycle)
paper_pattern: Prelims has two objective papers of 100 questions and 200 marks each (2 hours each): Paper I General Studies (humanities side), Paper II General Studies incl. science & technology, environment and mental ability. Prelims is screening only; marks are not counted in final merit.
remarks: The 2024 cycle (384 posts) was hit by a re-exam and irregularity allegations. Posts change every notification; confirm on the official site.
selection_process: Prelims (objective, screening) → Mains (5 descriptive papers + qualifying Kannada and English) → Personality test → Document verification

exam_name: Kerala PSC KAS (Kerala Administrative Service Officer Junior Time Scale Trainee Examination)
aliases: KAS Kerala; Kerala Administrative Service; Kerala PSC KAS Officer
eligibility: Bachelor's degree (incl. professional) in any subject. Stream 1 (open direct recruitment): age 21-32; Stream 2 (serving non-gazetted state employees): 21-40; Stream 3 (gazetted officers): under 50. Age relaxation for SC/ST (5 yrs), OBC (3 yrs), differently abled and others, max 50. Prelims Paper II tests Malayalam, Tamil or Kannada proficiency; officers who did not study Malayalam at matric level must later pass a Malayalam test.
test_date: Prelims: June (2025: 14 June); Mains: October (2025: 17-18 October)

remarks: Not held every year (2025 was the second KAS cycle). Only Stream 1 is open to fresh graduates; Streams 2 and 3 are for serving government employees.
selection_process: Prelims (objective, screening) → Mains (3 descriptive papers of 100 marks) → Interview (45 marks) → Document verification

exam_name: MPPSC SSE (Madhya Pradesh State Service Examination)
aliases: MPPSC; MP PCS; MPPSC State Service Exam; Rajya Sewa Pariksha
eligibility: Bachelor's degree; final-year students may apply. Age 21 to 40 for non-uniformed posts and 21 to 33 for uniformed posts (e.g. DSP) as on 1 Jan 2026; relaxations for MP domicile reserved categories. Candidates from other states can apply but are treated as unreserved; reservation only for MP domiciles.
application_fee: Rs. 500/- (Rs. 250/- for MP-domicile SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwD), plus portal charges
paper_pattern: Prelims has two objective papers, 2 hours each: Paper I General Studies (100 questions) and Paper II General Aptitude Test (100 questions, qualifying). Merit for mains is on Paper I only. Negative marking introduced from 2026.
remarks: Negative marking (one-third) was introduced for the first time in the 2026 prelims. Posts change every notification; confirm on the official site.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (descriptive, 1500 marks) → Interview (185 marks) → Document verification

exam_name: MPSC Rajyaseva (Maharashtra Gazetted Civil Services Combined Examination)
aliases: MPSC State Services; Rajyaseva; Maharashtra PCS; MPSC Gazetted Civil Services Combined Preliminary Exam
marking: -1/4 of the question's marks per wrong answer
eligibility: Bachelor's degree for most posts (some posts need specific degrees); final-year students may take prelims. Maximum age 38 for the open category, with relaxations for reserved categories and others. Adequate knowledge of Marathi is required; Marathi is a qualifying mains paper.
test_date: Prelims: May (2026: 31 May); Mains: as per notification
application_fee: Rs. 544/- (Rs. 344/- for reserved categories, EWS, orphans and PwBD) (2026 cycle)
paper_pattern: Prelims has two objective papers: Paper I General Studies (100 questions, 200 marks) and Paper II CSAT (80 questions, 200 marks, qualifying at 33%). Prelims marks only decide mains eligibility.
remarks: Vacancies are often raised by corrigenda after the notification. The 2026 mains was postponed; check mpsc.gov.in.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (9 descriptive papers, 1750 marks) → Interview (275 marks) → Document verification

exam_name: Manipur PSC CCE (Manipur Civil Services Combined Competitive Examination)
aliases: MCSCCE; Manipur PCS; Manipur Civil Service Exam; MPSC Manipur CCE
eligibility: Degree from a recognised university. Must be a permanent resident of Manipur (or have a parent/ancestor who was) and be able to speak Manipuri or a tribal dialect of Manipur. Age 21 to 38 (2022 cycle, as on 1 July 2022); relaxations for SC/ST (5 yrs), OBC (3 yrs), PwD (10 yrs).
application_fee: Rs. 600/- (Rs. 400/- for SC/ST; no fee for differently abled)
remarks: Held rarely: the 2022 cycle was the first in years (the 2019 exam was cancelled) and its mains ran into 2025-26. Check the official site for a new notification.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (written) → Interview/Personality test

exam_name: Meghalaya PSC CCE (Meghalaya Civil Service Examination)
aliases: MCS; Meghalaya Civil Service; Meghalaya PCS; MPSC Meghalaya
eligibility: Degree from any recognised university. Age 21 to 32 as on 1 Jan 2025; 5 years relaxation for SC/ST, more for PwD; no age bar for regular government employees who joined within age limit. Posts are reserved by Khasi-Jaintia, Garo and other categories; fee concession only for SC/ST permanent residents of Meghalaya.
test_date: As per notification (2025 advertisement: prelims 26 September 2026)
application_fee: Rs. 460/- (half for SC/ST permanent residents of Meghalaya; PwBD exempt)
paper_pattern: Prelims: two compulsory objective papers of 200 marks each, 2 hours each; Paper II is qualifying (33%).
remarks: Not held every year; posts depend on the advertisement. Confirm on the official site.
selection_process: Prelims (objective; 1:15 to mains) → Mains (7 descriptive papers incl. qualifying English) → Interview (150 marks)

exam_name: Mizoram PSC CCE (Mizoram Civil Services Combined Competitive Examination)
aliases: MCS Mizoram; Mizoram Civil Service; Mizoram PCS; MPSC Mizoram CCE
eligibility: Degree from a recognised university. Must be a permanent resident of Mizoram (or have a parent/ancestor who was), have basic computer knowledge, and pass the qualifying Mizo Language Proficiency test. Age 21 to 35 as on 1 Aug 2025; relaxations for SC/ST/OBC, ex-servicemen and PwBD.
application_fee: As prescribed by the Commission (PwBD exempt)
remarks: Posts are Group A Junior Grade posts in MCS, MPS, Finance & Accounts and Information services. Not held on a fixed yearly calendar.
selection_process: Prelims (objective, screening) → Mains (written) → Interview

exam_name: NPSC CCE (Nagaland Civil Service, Police Service & Allied Services Examination)
aliases: NCS NPS & Allied Services Exam; Nagaland PCS; NPSC Combined Competitive Examination
eligibility: Bachelor's degree in any discipline (incl. Divinity). Age 21 to 32 as on 1 Jan 2025; 5 years relaxation for SC/ST and up to 5 years for serving government employees. Reserved posts need an Indigenous Inhabitants of Nagaland or backward-tribe certificate; others are considered only for unreserved posts.
paper_pattern: Prelims is one common General Studies objective paper (2025 advertisement). The pattern was revised for later cycles; check the current notification.
remarks: Covers posts from EAC and DSP down to Class-III assistant posts. Exam pattern changed from 2026; confirm on the official site.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (written) → Physical test (some posts) → Interview → Document verification

aliases: OCS; Odisha PCS; OAS exam; Odisha Civil Service Exam
marking: -1/3 of the question's marks per wrong answer
eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university. Age 21 to 42 as on 1 Jan 2025; 5 years relaxation for SC/ST/SEBC/women/ex-servicemen, 10 for PwD. Must be able to read, write and speak Odia (e.g. Odia passed up to Class VII/middle school). Attempt limits apply (6 for general).
test_date: Prelims: June (7 June 2026); Mains: as per notification
paper_pattern: Prelims has two objective papers of 200 marks each, 2 hours each: GS Paper I and GS Paper II (CSAT, qualifying at 33%). Prelims marks not counted for final merit.
remarks: The first notice had no OAS/OFS/ORS posts; an addendum added OAS and ORS posts. Posts change every notification.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (9 descriptive papers, incl. qualifying Odia and English) → Interview (250 marks) → Document verification

exam_name: PPSC PCS (Punjab State Civil Services Combined Competitive Examination)
aliases: Punjab PCS; PSCSCCE; PPSC Civil Services; Punjab Civil Service Exam
eligibility: Bachelor's degree (final-year students may take prelims). Must have passed Matriculation with Punjabi as a subject or equivalent. Age 21 to 37 as on 1 Jan 2025 (21 to 28 for DSP and Deputy Superintendent Jails); relaxations up to 42 for SC/BC of Punjab and others.
test_date: As per notification (2025 prelims held 7 December 2025 after rescheduling)
application_fee: Rs. 1500/- (Rs. 750/- for SC/ST and BC of Punjab; Rs. 500/- for ex-servicemen, EWS, PwD, LDESM of Punjab)
paper_pattern: Prelims has two objective papers of 200 marks, 2 hours each: Paper I General Studies (100 questions x 2 marks) and Paper II CSAT (80 questions x 2.5 marks, qualifying at 40%). Merit on Paper I only; no negative marking.
remarks: Matric-level Punjabi is compulsory. Posts change every notification; confirm on the official site.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (7 descriptive papers incl. Punjabi and English) → Interview (150 marks) → Document verification

exam_name: RPSC RAS (Rajasthan State and Subordinate Services Combined Competitive Examination)
aliases: RAS; RTS; RAS/RTS; Rajasthan Administrative Service; RPSC RAS Pre
forms_out: May-June (2026: notification 27 May, applications from 4 June)
marking: 1/3 of the question's marks deducted per wrong answer (150 questions, 200 marks)
eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university. Age 21-40 years as on 1 January 2027; age relaxations for reserved categories and women as per Rajasthan rules. Lower fee for Rajasthan non-creamy-layer OBC/MBC, EWS, SC, ST and PwBD.
test_date: Prelims in December (6 December 2026 per RPSC exam calendar); Mains 1-2 May 2027
application_fee: Rs. 600/- (General, creamy-layer OBC/MBC); Rs. 400/- (Rajasthan non-creamy-layer OBC/MBC, EWS, SC, ST, PwBD)
paper_pattern: One objective paper on General Knowledge and General Science: 150 questions, 200 marks, 3 hours. It is a screening test; marks do not count in the final merit list.
remarks: Posts and dates change every notification; confirm on the official RPSC site.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (written) → Interview/personality test → Document verification & medical

exam_name: SPSC CCE (Sikkim Services Combined Recruitment Examination)
aliases: Sikkim PSC Under Secretary; Sikkim State Civil Service; SSCS; Sikkim Combined Competitive Examination; SPSC Under Secretary
eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university. Age 21-40 years as on 31 January 2026. Only local candidates: must hold a Sikkim Subject Certificate or Certificate of Identification and a valid Local Employment Card issued by the Sikkim government.
last_date: As per notification (31 January 2026 for the last advertisement)
remarks: Only Sikkim locals (Sikkim Subject / COI holders) can apply. The scheme and syllabus are published separately on the SPSC website.
selection_process: Written examination → Document scrutiny → Viva-voce

aliases: TNPSC Group I; CCSE-I; Tamil Nadu Group 1; TNPSC Deputy Collector exam
forms_out: June (2026: notification 23 June, applications from 30 June)
eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university. Minimum age 21; maximum 34 years for 'Others' and 39 years for SC, SC(A), ST, MBC/DC, BC, BCM and destitute widows for most posts (as on 1 July 2026; a few posts differ). Mains includes a compulsory Tamil Eligibility Test paper.
test_date: September (2026 prelims 27 September, moved from 6 September); 2025 prelims was 15 June
application_fee: One-time registration Rs. 150/-; prelims fee Rs. 100/-; mains fee Rs. 200/- (no fee for SC, SC(A), ST, PwBD, destitute widows; limited free chances for MBC/DNC, BC, BCM and ex-servicemen)
paper_pattern: One objective paper of 3 hours: General Studies (175 questions, 250 marks) and Aptitude & Mental Ability (25 questions, 50 marks), 200 questions and 300 marks in all. Screening only; not counted in the final merit list.
remarks: Tamil knowledge is needed to clear the Mains Tamil eligibility paper. Vacancies often rise through addenda after the notification.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (Tamil eligibility paper + 3 GS papers) → Interview → Document verification

aliases: TNPSC Group IV; CCSE-IV; TNPSC VAO; TNPSC Junior Assistant; TNPSC Typist; Group 4
forms_out: October (2026: 6 October); 2025 cycle notified in April
eligibility: Class 10 (SSLC) pass for most posts (VAO, Junior Assistant, Bill Collector etc.); Typist and Steno-Typist posts also need typewriting/shorthand qualifications. Minimum age 18 (21 for VAO, Forest Guard and Forest Watcher) as on 1 July 2026; upper age limits differ by post and community, so check the notification. Part A is a Tamil eligibility test, so Tamil is needed.
test_date: January 2027 (10 January) for the 2026 notification; 2025 exam was 12 July 2025
application_fee: Rs. 100/- exam fee, plus Rs. 150/- one-time registration for new users (exemptions for eligible categories as per TNPSC rules)
paper_pattern: One OMR paper, 3 hours, 200 questions, 300 marks: Part A Tamil Eligibility-cum-Scoring Test (100 questions, 150 marks, at least 60 marks needed); Part B General Studies (75 questions) and Part C Aptitude & Mental Ability (25 questions), 150 marks together. Parts B and C are evaluated only if Part A is cleared.
remarks: Single written exam with no interview; posts include VAO, Junior Assistant, Typist and Tax Collector. Vacancy numbers often rise after the notification.
selection_process: Written exam (OMR) → Certificate verification → Counselling & post allocation

aliases: TSPSC Group 1; TGPSC Group I; Telangana Group 1; Telangana State PSC Group 1
eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university (some posts need specific degrees, e.g. mechanical/automobile engineering for RTO). Age 18-46 years for most posts; 21-35 for DSP and Assistant Excise Superintendent, 18-35 for Deputy Superintendent of Jails (2024 notification). Relaxations as per Telangana rules.
application_fee: Rs. 200/- application processing fee + Rs. 120/- exam fee (exam fee exemption for some groups such as unemployed applicants, as per notification)
paper_pattern: One objective paper, General Studies and Mental Ability: 150 questions, 150 marks, 2.5 hours. Screening test for Mains.
remarks: No new Group 1 notification had been issued as of November 2026; the last one (2024) had 563 posts.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (6 descriptive papers of 150 marks) → Document verification

exam_name: TPSC TCS/TPS (Tripura Civil Service and Tripura Police Service Grade-II Examination)
aliases: TCS Grade II; TPS Grade II; Tripura Civil Service; Tripura Police Service; TPSC TCS
marking: 1/4 of the question's marks deducted per wrong or multiple answer
eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university; knowledge of Bengali/English/Kokborok is desirable. Age 21-40 years (as on 1 March 2022 for the last advertisement); 5 years relaxation for SC, ST, PwBD and government servants. SC/ST candidates of other states apply as general.
last_date: As per notification (30 April 2022 for Advt. 05/2022)
test_date: As per notification (Advt. 05/2022 prelims held 2 April 2023)
paper_pattern: One objective, OMR-based screening test of 200 marks. Marks do not count in the final merit list; up to 10 times the posts (category-wise) are called for Mains.
remarks: Notifications are irregular; the last TCS/TPS Grade-II advertisement found was in 2022. Check the TPSC site for new ones.
selection_process: Prelims (objective, 200 marks) → Mains (written, 800 marks; includes Bengali/Alternative English/Kokborok paper) → Personality test (100 marks) → Medical

exam_name: UPPSC PCS (Combined State/Upper Subordinate Services Examination)
aliases: UP PCS; UPPCS; Uttar Pradesh PCS; UPPSC Combined State Upper Subordinate Services
marking: 1/3 of the question's marks deducted per wrong answer
eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university; some posts need specific degrees (e.g. LLB, postgraduate maths/statistics). Age 21-40 years as on 1 July 2026; relaxations for reserved categories as per UP rules. Final-year students may apply.
application_fee: Rs. 125/- (General/EWS/OBC, incl. Rs. 25/- processing fee); Rs. 65/- (SC/ST, ex-servicemen); Rs. 25/- (PwBD)
paper_pattern: Two objective papers of 2 hours each: General Studies Paper I (150 questions, 200 marks) and CSAT Paper II (100 questions, 200 marks, qualifying at 33%). Only Paper I decides who goes to Mains.
remarks: Vacancies can change a lot before results (2025 rose from about 200 to 920); confirm on the official site.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (written) → Interview → Document verification

exam_name: UKPSC PCS (Uttarakhand Combined State Civil/Upper Subordinate Services Examination)
aliases: Uttarakhand PCS; UKPSC Upper PCS; Upper PCS; UK PCS
marking: 1/4 of the question's marks deducted per wrong or multiple answer
eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university (some posts need specific or postgraduate degrees). Age 21-42 years as on 1 July 2026; relaxations as per Uttarakhand rules. Reserved-category and fee concessions are for Uttarakhand categories. Mains has a compulsory General Hindi paper (35% minimum).
application_fee: Rs. 166.36/- (Unreserved, Uttarakhand OBC, EWS); Rs. 76.36/- (Uttarakhand SC/ST, PwBD); no fee for Uttarakhand orphans
paper_pattern: Paper I General Studies: 150 questions, 150 marks, 2 hours, at least 1/3 of questions on Uttarakhand. Paper II General Aptitude: 100 questions, 150 marks, 2 hours, qualifying (33%). Mains shortlist is based on Paper I.
remarks: Mains includes two papers on Uttarakhand and a General Hindi paper, so Hindi is needed.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (8 written papers, 1500 marks) → Interview/personality test (150 marks) → Document verification & medical

exam_name: WBCS (West Bengal Civil Service Executive etc. Examination)
aliases: WBCS Exe; WBPSC WBCS; West Bengal Civil Service; WBCS Executive
forms_out: As per notification (WBCS 2024 exam: notified 14 November 2025)
marking: +1 per question; negative marking applies (see notification for the deduction)
eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university. Must be able to read, write and speak Bengali (not required if the mother tongue is Nepali). Minimum age 21 (20 for Group B police); upper limit varies by group (A, B, C, D) and sources conflict, so check the notification. Relaxations for SC/ST, OBC of West Bengal and PwBD.
last_date: As per notification (December 2025 for the 2024 exam)
test_date: As per notification (WBCS 2024 prelims held 14 June 2026)
application_fee: Rs. 210/- plus service charges (no fee for SC/ST of West Bengal and PwBD 40%+)
paper_pattern: One objective paper: 200 questions, 200 marks, 2.5 hours; 8 subjects of 25 questions each (English, General Science, Current Events, History of India, Geography of India with West Bengal focus, Polity & Economy, Indian National Movement, General Mental Ability). Screening only.
remarks: Exam years lag behind: the 'WBCS 2024' exam was notified in late 2025 and its prelims held in June 2026. Bengali is required for most candidates.
selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (written; Groups A & B add an optional subject) → Personality test → Document verification

exam_name: UPSSSC PET (Uttar Pradesh Preliminary Eligibility Test)
aliases: UP PET; PET; UPSSSC Preliminary Eligibility Test
marking: +1 per correct answer; negative marking applies (see the notification)
eligibility: Class 10 pass (higher qualifications can also apply). Age 18-40 years as on 1 July 2026; relaxations for reserved categories as per UP rules. The score is valid for 3 years.
application_fee: Rs. 185/- (General/OBC, incl. Rs. 25/- processing fee); Rs. 95/- (SC/ST); Rs. 25/- (PwBD)
paper_pattern: One objective paper: 100 questions, 100 marks, 2 hours, covering history, geography, polity, general science, arithmetic, Hindi, English, reasoning and general awareness.
remarks: PET is not a job by itself; it is needed to apply for most UPSSSC Group C posts, which shortlist on PET score.
selection_process: PET (eligibility test) → Shortlisting on PET score for post-wise UPSSSC main exams → Main exam → Document verification

exam_name: UP Police Constable (Uttar Pradesh Police Constable Recruitment)
aliases: UPPRPB Constable; UPPBPB Constable; UP Police Sipahi; UP Constable and Jail Warder; UP Police Bharti
eligibility: Class 12 pass (appearing candidates not eligible). Age 18-22 years for men and 18-25 for women (general category, as on 1 July 2025 for the 2025 cycle); relaxations exist for SC/ST/OBC, UP government employees and ex-servicemen. Height: men 168 cm (160 cm ST), women 152 cm (147 cm ST); men's chest 79-84 cm (5 cm expansion). Reservation benefits are for UP residents.
paper_pattern: One objective paper of 150 questions for 300 marks (2 marks each) in 2 hours, covering General Knowledge, General Hindi, Numerical and Mental Ability, Mental Aptitude, Intelligence and Reasoning. Minimum marks to qualify: 30% UR, 25% EWS/OBC, 20% SC/ST.
remarks: One Time Registration (OTR) on the UPPRPB portal is needed before applying. Posts and age limits change every notification; confirm on uppbpb.gov.in.
selection_process: Written exam (OMR) → Document verification & Physical Standard Test (height, chest) → Physical Efficiency Test (run: men 4.8 km in 25 min, women 2.4 km in 14 min; qualifying) → Merit list on written marks → Medical exam & character verification

exam_name: UP Police SI (Uttar Pradesh Police Sub-Inspector Recruitment)
aliases: UPPRPB SI; UP SI Civil Police; UP Daroga; UP Police Sub Inspector and Platoon Commander
eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university. Age 21-28 years (general category); relaxations exist for reserved categories. Height: men 168 cm (160 cm ST), women 152 cm (147 cm ST); men's chest 79-84 cm with 5 cm expansion; women minimum 40 kg. Reservation benefits are for UP residents.
paper_pattern: One objective paper of 160 questions in four sections of 40 each (General Hindi; Law/Constitution and General Knowledge; Numerical and Mental Ability; Mental Aptitude, Intelligence and Reasoning), 2 hours.
remarks: One Time Registration on the UPPRPB portal is needed. The 2025 cycle covers SI Civil Police, Platoon Commander PAC and equivalent posts; confirm current status on uppbpb.gov.in.
selection_process: Written exam → Document verification & Physical Standard Test → Physical Efficiency Test (run: men 4.8 km in 28 min, women 2.4 km in 16 min; qualifying) → Merit list → Medical exam

exam_name: Bihar Police Constable (CSBC Bihar Police Constable Recruitment)
aliases: CSBC Constable; Bihar Sipahi Bharti; Bihar Police Sipahi; CSBC Bihar Police and BSAP Constable
eligibility: Class 12 (Intermediate) pass, or Maulvi/Shastri/Acharya or equivalent recognised by the Bihar government. Age (2025 cycle): general 18-25; OBC up to 27 (men)/28 (women); SC/ST up to 30; other relaxations exist. Height: men 165 cm (General/BC), 160 cm (EBC/SC/ST); women 155 cm. Men's chest 81-86 cm (79-84 cm SC/ST). Reservation, including 35% for women, is for Bihar residents.
application_fee: Rs. 675/- (Rs. 180/- for SC/ST, women and transgender candidates of Bihar)
paper_pattern: One objective paper of 100 questions for 100 marks in 2 hours at Class 10 (Bihar Board) level: Hindi, English, Mathematics, Science, Social Science, General Knowledge and Current Affairs. Qualifying (30% minimum).
remarks: PET is called at about five times the vacancies. CSBC also runs separate drives for Driver Constable, Special Branch and Prohibition Constable; check csbc.bihar.gov.in.
selection_process: Written exam (qualifying) → Physical Standard Test (height, chest) → Physical Efficiency Test (100 marks: run 1.6 km men / 1 km women, shot put, high jump) → Merit list → Document verification → Medical exam

exam_name: Bihar Police SI (BPSSC Bihar Police Sub-Inspector Recruitment)
aliases: BPSSC SI; Bihar Daroga; Bihar Police Daroga Bharti; Police Sub-Inspector Bihar
eligibility: Graduation from a recognised university by 1 Aug 2025. Minimum age 20 (on 1 Aug 2025); maximum (on 1 Aug 2024) 37 for unreserved men, 40 for unreserved women and BC/EBC, 42 for SC/ST and third gender. Height: men 165 cm (UR/BC), 160 cm (EBC/SC/ST); women 155 cm. Men's chest 81/86 cm (79/84 cm SC/ST); women at least 48 kg. Reservation, including 35% for women, is for Bihar residents.
paper_pattern: Prelims: one objective paper of 100 questions for 200 marks in 2 hours on General Knowledge and Current Affairs; 30% minimum; 0.2 marks cut per wrong answer. Candidates up to 20 times the vacancies go to the Mains.
remarks: Final merit is based only on Mains marks; PET is pass/fail. BPSSC cancelled the 2025-cycle Mains on 23 Sept 2026, so check bpssc.bihar.gov.in for the re-exam.
selection_process: Prelims (objective, qualifying) → Mains: Paper 1 General Hindi (qualifying, 30%) + Paper 2 General Studies (200 marks) → Physical Efficiency Test & PST (qualifying: run men 1.6 km in 6:30 / women 1 km in 6 min, high jump, long jump, shot put) → Document verification & medical → Merit on Mains marks

exam_name: Maharashtra Police Bharti (Maharashtra Police Constable Recruitment)
aliases: Maharashtra Police Shipai Bharti; Police Constable Maharashtra; Mahapolice Bharti; SRPF Constable; Karagruh Shipai
eligibility: Class 12 (HSC) pass. Age 18-28 years (open category); reserved categories get relaxation, and the 2025 drive gave a one-time chance to those who crossed the age limit in 2022-2023. Height: men 165 cm, women 155 cm. Applicants should be residents of Maharashtra.
paper_pattern: Written test of 100 objective questions for 100 marks in 90 minutes, in Marathi: Mathematics, General Knowledge and Current Affairs, Intellectual (reasoning) test and Marathi Grammar. Minimum 40% to qualify.
remarks: Recruitment is run unit-wise (district/commissionerate) through one state portal; candidates apply to one unit per post. Confirm dates on mahapolice.gov.in.
selection_process: Physical Standard Test (height, chest) → Physical test (50 marks: men 1600 m run, 100 m run, shot put; women 800 m run, 100 m run, shot put; min 50%) → Written exam (100 marks, called at 1:10 of vacancies) → Driving/skill test for Driver and Bandsman → Document verification & medical

exam_name: Rajasthan Police Constable (Rajasthan Police Constable Recruitment)
aliases: Rajasthan Police Sipahi; Rajasthan Constable GD; Rajasthan Police Constable Bharti
eligibility: Class 12 pass and a valid RSSB Common Eligibility Test (Senior Secondary level) score with at least 40% (35% SC/ST). Age: 18-23 for general men, 18-28 for general women; relaxations exist for reserved categories. Height: men 168 cm, women 152 cm; men's chest also measured. Out-of-state candidates can apply in the general fee category.
application_fee: Rs. 600/- (Rs. 400/- for OBC/MBC non-creamy layer, EWS, SC, ST of Rajasthan)
paper_pattern: Objective written test of 150 marks on Reasoning and Computer basics, General Knowledge/Science/Current Affairs, and Rajasthan GK. See the notification for the number of questions, time and negative marking.
remarks: A CET (Senior Secondary) pass from RSSB is needed before you can apply. Posts are split district-wise and by TSP/non-TSP areas.
selection_process: Written exam → Physical Efficiency Test (5 km run: men 25 min, women 35 min; qualifying) & Physical Standard Test → Special/proficiency marks → Merit list → Document verification → Medical exam

exam_name: MP Police Constable (MPESB Madhya Pradesh Police Constable GD Recruitment)
aliases: MPESB Constable; MP Police Aarakshak Bharti; MP Constable GD; Police Constable Recruitment Test (PCRT)
eligibility: Class 10 pass (Class 8 for ST candidates); live registration at an MP employment office. Age 18-33 for MP unreserved/EWS men and other-state candidates; up to 38 for women and MP reserved-category men; further relaxations exist. Candidates from other states can apply only as unreserved. Height: men 168 cm (160 cm ST), women 155 cm; men's chest 81/86 cm (76/81 cm ST). SAF posts are for men only.
application_fee: Rs. 500/- exam fee + Rs. 200/- department fee (MP SC/ST/OBC/EWS: Rs. 250/- + Rs. 100/-), plus MP Online portal fee
paper_pattern: Online test of 100 objective questions for 100 marks in 2 hours (Hindi/English): General Knowledge and Reasoning 40, Intellectual Ability and Mental Aptitude 30, Science and Simple Arithmetic 30. No negative marking.
remarks: PET marks count in the final merit, so physical preparation matters. Candidates are called to PET at up to 7 times the vacancies.
selection_process: Computer-based written exam → Physical Efficiency Test (100 marks: 800 m run, long jump, shot put; min 30) → Physical measurement & document verification → Medical exam → Merit on written + PET marks

exam_name: WB Police Constable (WBPRB West Bengal Police Constable Recruitment)
aliases: WBPRB Constable; West Bengal Police Constable; WBP Constable; WBP Lady Constable
eligibility: Madhyamik (Class 10) pass. Age 18-30 years (as on 1 Jan 2024 for the 2024 drive); relaxations for SC/ST (5 yrs), OBC-A/B (3 yrs) and others. Must speak, read and write Bengali (except residents of Darjeeling and Kalimpong hill sub-divisions). Height: men 167 cm (160 cm for Gorkha, Garhwali, Rajbanshi, ST), women 160 cm (152 cm); men's chest 78/83 cm (76/81 cm); minimum weights apply.
application_fee: Rs. 170/- (Rs. 150/- + Rs. 20/- processing; SC/ST of West Bengal pay only Rs. 20/-)
paper_pattern: One OMR paper of 85 objective questions for 85 marks in 1 hour: General Awareness and GK 25, English 10, Elementary Mathematics (Madhyamik level) 25, Reasoning 25. 1/4 mark cut per wrong answer; question paper in Bengali and Nepali.
remarks: Merit is written plus interview marks out of 100. Kolkata Police runs its own constable recruitment through the same board.
selection_process: Written exam (85 marks) → Physical Measurement Test (qualifying) → Physical Efficiency Test (men 1600 m in 6 min 30 s, women 800 m in 4 min; qualifying) → Interview (15 marks) → Medical exam

exam_name: TN Police Constable (TNUSRB Grade II Police Constable Recruitment)
aliases: TNUSRB PC; Tamil Nadu Grade II Constable; TNUSRB Common Recruitment; Jail Warder and Fireman
eligibility: Class 10 (SSLC) pass. Age 18-26 for OC (as on 1 July 2025); up to 28 for BC/MBC, 31 for SC/ST and transgender, 37 for destitute widows; other relaxations exist. Height: men 170 cm (167 cm SC/ST), women 159 cm (157 cm SC/ST); men's chest 81-86 cm. A Tamil language test must be passed.
paper_pattern: OMR written exam in two parts: a qualifying Tamil language paper (40% needed) and a main paper on General Knowledge and Psychology; only the main paper counts for merit.
remarks: One common recruitment fills Grade II Police Constable, Jail Warder and Fireman posts; candidates give post preferences. Confirm the official notification at tnusrb.tn.gov.in.
selection_process: Written exam (Tamil eligibility + main paper) → Certificate verification, Physical Measurement Test, Endurance Test and Physical Efficiency Test → Special marks (NCC/sports etc.) → Provisional selection list → Medical exam

exam_name: Karnataka Police Constable (KSP Civil Police Constable Recruitment)
aliases: KSP CPC; Karnataka Civil Police Constable; KSP Constable Civil; Karnataka Police Peda
eligibility: PUC (Class 12) pass or equivalent. Age 18-33 for general merit; up to 35 for SC/ST/Cat-1/2A/2B/3A/3B; up to 38 for forest-area tribal candidates. Must have studied Kannada in SSLC or pass a Kannada language test. Height: men 168 cm, women 157 cm (155/150 cm for forest-area tribal candidates); men's chest 86 cm expanded with 5 cm expansion; women at least 45 kg.
application_fee: Rs. 750/- (Rs. 500/- for SC/ST/Cat-1, ex-servicemen, third gender)
paper_pattern: Written exam of 100 objective questions for 100 marks in 90 minutes: General Knowledge, Science, Geography, History, Indian Constitution, Current Affairs, Ethics and Mental Ability. 0.25 mark cut per wrong answer; minimum 30 marks.
remarks: Separate notifications for the Kalyana Karnataka (371-J) cadre and the rest of the state; posts are allotted by police unit. Applications are handled by KEA.
selection_process: Written exam (min 30/100) → Physical Standard Test → Endurance Test (men: 1600 m in 6 min 30 s, high/long jump, shot put; women: 400 m in 2 min, high/long jump, shot put) → Medical exam & document verification

exam_name: Gujarat Lokrakshak (GPRB Gujarat Police Lokrakshak Recruitment)
aliases: Gujarat LRD; Lokrakshak Dal; Gujarat Police Constable; GPRB LRD; Unarmed/Armed Police Constable; SRPF Constable Gujarat; Jail Sepoy
eligibility: Class 12 (Higher Secondary) pass. Age 18-33 years (general); relaxation of 5 years for general women and reserved men, 10 years for reserved women (max 45), plus ex-servicemen rules. Reservation only for original residents of Gujarat. Must know Gujarati or Hindi and basic computer use. Height: men 165 cm (162 cm for ST of Gujarat), chest 79/84 cm; women 155 cm (150 cm ST).
test_date: Physical test January; written exam June
application_fee: Rs. 100/- (no fee for EWS, SC, ST, SEBC and ex-servicemen)
paper_pattern: Objective MCQ test of 200 questions for 200 marks in 3 hours. Part A (80): Reasoning and Data Interpretation 30, Quantitative Aptitude 30, Gujarati comprehension 20. Part B (120): Constitution 30, Current Affairs/Science/GK 40, History, Culture and Geography of Gujarat and India 50. 40% needed in each part; 0.25 cut per wrong or blank answer (option E = not attempted, no penalty).
remarks: The physical test comes first and is pass/fail; merit is the written score plus any bonus marks. One form can cover both the PSI and Lokrakshak cadres.
selection_process: Physical Efficiency Test (run: men 5000 m in 25 min, women 1600 m in 9 min 30 s; qualifying) → Physical Standard Test (height, chest) → Written MCQ test (200 marks) + bonus marks (NCC C, RRU/NFSU, sports) → Document verification → Medical exam
